summary.tagline: The Gargano National Park (Italian: Parco nazionale del Gargano) is a national park in the province of Foggia

days.title: Northern Lakes and Geological Wonders
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Punta Pietre Nere
stops.detail: An exception is Punta Pietre Nere, a mass of dark volcanic rocks dating back to the Triassic, outcropping on the beach of Lesina.

stops.name: dolina Pozzatina
stops.detail: The Pozzatina sinkhole, more than 100 meters deep and with a diameter of about 500, is the largest in Europe (the sinkhole is part of the Municipality of San Nicandro Garganico).

stops.name: lago di Lesina
stops.detail: Lake Lesina, 24.4 km long and 2.4 km wide, has a perimeter of almost 50 km and is to all intents and purposes a lagoon.

stops.name: lago di Varano
stops.detail: Lake Varano is the largest in southern Italy (60.5 km²).

days.title: Southern Wetlands and Mountain Forests
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: lago Salso
stops.detail: Lake Salso (5.5 km²), located near Manfredonia and fed by the Cervaro river, is characterized instead by its fresh waters.

stops.name: Oasi Lago Salso
stops.detail: The lake area, due to its great relevance in the field of biodiversity, is part of the Lake Salso Oasis, managed in collaboration with WWF Italy.

stops.name: Monte Sacro
stops.detail: Other woods of naturalistic interest are also those of Monte Sant'Angelo, of Monte Sacro (Mattinata), of Spina Pulci (between San Nicandro Garganico and Cagnano Varano.
